chunks: And from him, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Burayd al-Ajli, who said:

I asked him about a man who manumitted his slave by installments (mukatab) for one thousand dirhams, and did not stipulate at the time of the contract that if he became unable to pay, he would return to slavery. And the mukatab paid his master five hundred dirhams, then the mukatab died, leaving wealth, and leaving a mature son.
He said: 'Half of whatever the mukatab left is for his master who contracted with him, and the remaining half is for the son of the mukatab.

Because the mukatab died, and half of him was free and half of him was a slave to the one who contracted with him. So the son of the mukatab is in the same state as his father: half of him is free and half of him is a slave to the one who contracted with his father.
If he pays to the one who contracted with his father what remained on his father, then he is free, and there is no claim of anyone among the people upon him.'

key_terms.رَدٌّ فِي الرِّقِّ: Return to slavery (if unable to pay)
key_terms.مكاتب: A slave who has entered into a contract of manumission by installments

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling for a mukatab (slave under manumission contract) who dies before paying the full amount?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the legal status of a *mukatab* (slave with a manumission contract) who dies before fulfilling the agreement, establishing the principle of 'half-free, half-slave' (*nisfun hurrin wa nisfun abdin*). It highlights the practical implication that the son inherits this dual status, allowing him to secure full emancipation by settling the remaining debt, thereby preserving the family's lineage and economic stability within the Shia jurisprudence of *kitabah*.
